text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Nigeria has not drawn up plans to leave the Commonwealth of Britain and its former colonies, from which it is suspended, says special adviser to the head of state Auwalu Yadudu. He described as "false" local reports suggesting that Nigeria planned to leave.

- Information Minister Walter Ofonagoro describes the majority state-owned Daily Times DTIM.LG newspaper as "sick" and says that the company is on the verge of bankruptcy. He said the government would not provide any money to bail it out until the cause of its problems is unearthed.
- Sources at the central bank say it has shortlisted two consultants to install computers and plan reform of the clearing house.
- Nigeria will take no new foreign loans until the bulk of its external debt, estimated at over $28 billion, is redeemed, says Finance Minister Anthony Ani.
- State-run Nigerian Telecommunications will this year spend 11 billion naira of internally generated revenue on expansion projects, says Communications Minister Major-General Tajudeen Olanrewaju.
- Nigeria's primary education system will require 80 billion naira to put it in proper shape, says the secretary-general of the National Primary Education Commission.

- Repairing Nigeria's oil refineries to a level where they are working at 85 percent of their 445,000 barrel per day capacity would cost 86 billion naira spread over a period of 18 months, says Petroleum Minister Dan Etete.
- British financial institution seals London office of Nigeria Airways at Heathrow Airport and confiscates company assets over a $31 million debt.
